title: Non-inverse monomials with the minimum even-dimensional vanishing-flat count
summary: Determine whether an even-dimensional non-APN monomial outside the inverse family can attain the sharp lower bound on its number of vanishing flats.

formal_statement.body: Let $n$ be even and let $F_d(x)=x^d$ be a non-APN monomial on $\mathbb F_{2^n}$. Exclude the inverse function's Frobenius equivalence orbit, namely exponents $d\equiv-2^i\pmod{2^n-1}$ for $0\le i<n$, as prescribed by Remark II.2 and the source's Table II convention. Determine whether some remaining exponent satisfies $$|\operatorname{VB}_{n,d}|=\frac{2^n-1}{3}.$$ A positive answer requires one verified exponent outside that orbit; a negative answer must prove that every attaining monomial in every even dimension belongs to the inverse orbit.

scope.domain: Vanishing flats of monomial functions over binary finite fields
assumptions: Frobenius variants of the inverse function are treated as one source-stated equivalence family
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result constructs an attaining monomial outside the inverse Frobenius orbit or proves that the inverse orbit contains every attaining monomial in all even dimensions.

citations.label: Li--Meidl--Polujan--Pott--Riera--Stanica, even-dimensional vanishing-flat question
citations.locator: Concluding remarks, item (1), journal p. 7110; Remark II.2 and the Table II convention

progress.summary: After proving the even-dimensional lower bound sharp for the inverse function, the source asks whether any other monomial attains it; its equivalence conventions exclude trivial Frobenius variants.
